title: Shrewsbury end of the line and streetcar rides to Spanish Fort
summary: Shrewsbury was just a small community at the end of the line; Saturday rides to Spanish Fort were a major amusement.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well what was in Shrewsbury then?

It wasn't nothing in Shrewsbury. I don't know how. It was just the end of the line. It was just the end of the line. It was just the end of the line. I see, I just wanted to have some homes and stuff where people would go after. Yeah, it was a little community they called Shrewsbury, you know, just like they called Harryhann and Kenner up there. Shrewsbury was a little development there or something. And then people lived out there though.
Would you ride the streetcars just to take a ride?

Well sometimes in those days, yeah, it was quite a deal. Amusement? Yeah, like I said, people would take that ride out the Spanish Fort just to, you know, go take a streetcar ride all the way out from Canal Street in town all the way out to the west.
How long would it take to get from Canal Street up to the Spanish Fort?

Oh, I imagine it would take about 45 minutes, I imagine, you know. You know, when we used to... Maybe an hour even, you know, because they used to stop, they used to make stops, you know, you know. They didn't make every stop at the streetcars. They stopped at the main at the section. If they were filled up, they didn't stop. I don't think they remember that.

When my mother would talk to me when I was a little boy, she'd say, Oh, well when we went for a ride, that was a big thing just to go for a ride. Well, that's right, yeah. You know, and people were easily amused, you know. They didn't have anything to do.
Just to look at... They didn't have TV. They didn't have radio. They didn't TV, like that. If you go out on a Saturday and take a ride out to the lake, I mean, it was a big deal.
